answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than cheap identities. Like a tide that lifts only anchored boats, peers weight an agent's signal by its history of completed, attested transactions, not by how many accounts it spawns. Newcomers start on a small island of low-trust tasks and earn broader access only as their record grows, so flooding the network with fake identities buys nothing.
